text: The city opened its bike share in 2019 with forty stations and four hundred bikes. Riders took more trips every year, and the busiest month was always June. - Bikes are easy to find near the station
- The app works well
- Some docks are often full

Add twenty stations.
Open at six.

Each station has room for twelve bikes and a screen that shows the nearest dock. The council pays for the docks, and a private firm runs the fleet on contract. Repairs take two days on average, and a van moves bikes from full stations at night. Electric bikes were added in 2022 and now make up a third of all trips. A yearly pass costs sixty euros, and a single ride costs one euro.

Surveys show that nine in ten riders would recommend the service to a friend. The main complaint is that docks near the station are often full in the morning. Crime is low: fewer than twenty bikes a year are stolen or lost. The firm proposes forty new stations in the outer districts by 2027.
